scope: Bounded linguistic, feminist and early-1990s reply-cluster argument audit, supplementing the sole Gareth researcher; not a second full-person dossier.
primary_body_rule: Only reading extents stated below are claimed. Metadata verification and named-reader accounts do not silently become direct primary argument reading.
reply_target_guard: Lawrence and Miles Taylor (1993) principally reply to Mayfield and Thorne while offering their own bounded Jones critique. Joyce (1993) names both pairs in his title but body is unread. Jones (1996) reply-to-Joyce/Vernon claim remains unverified because substantive primary body was not obtained.

rows.citation: Patrick Joyce, Visions of the People: Industrial England and the Question of Class, 1848–1914 (Cambridge University Press, 1991).
rows.reading_extent: Fresh selected primary p. 10 in publisher PDF; visual collation. Whole book unread.
rows.argument_assessment: Balances acknowledgment of Jones’s innovation with explicit methodological criticism.

rows.citation: Patrick Joyce, Democratic Subjects: The Self and the Social in Nineteenth-Century England (Cambridge University Press, 1994).
rows.reading_extent: Fresh selected introduction pp. 4–7 via publisher preview OCR; whole book unread.
rows.argument_assessment: Develops social/democratic imaginaries, questions Thompson’s experiential sequence, and credits Scott/Riley. Jones appears among examples of histories of class, not as a newly established direct critical target in the selected passage.
rows.endpoint_status: patrick_joyce exists; no further Gareth claim.
locators: Introduction pp. 4–7; p. 6 note 12, p. 7 note 13.

rows.citation: James Vernon, Politics and the People: A Study in English Political Culture,c.1815–1867 (Cambridge University Press, 1993).
rows.reading_extent: Fresh selected primary introduction p. 4; visual collation. Whole book unread.
rows.argument_assessment: Names specific limits while crediting Jones as a catalyst.

rows.citation: James Vernon, “Who’s Afraid of the ‘Linguistic Turn’? The Politics of Social History and Its Discontents,” Social History19(1)( 1994),81–97.
rows.reading_extent: Publisher/DOI metadata only; primary article body not obtained.
rows.argument_assessment: Title establishes participation in debate, not a verified direct criticism of Jones or the details of the argument.
rows.endpoint_status: james_vernon exists, but no edge inferred.

rows.citation: Anna Clark, “The Rhetoric of Chartist Domesticity: Gender, Language, and Class in the 1830 s and 1840 s,” Journal of British Studies31(1)(January 1992),62–88.
rows.reading_extent: Fresh publisher-displayed opening extract and notes 6–7; remaining article unread.
rows.argument_assessment: Explicitly follows Jones in treating domestic rhetoric as politically productive rather than a simple economic reflection. Develops a gender question; not evidence of a blanket anti-Jones camp.
rows.endpoint_status: Anna Clark has no node. Alice Clark and Darlene Clark Hine are different people.

rows.citation: Anna Clark, The Struggle for the Breeches: Gender and the Making of the British Working Class (University of California Press, 1995).
rows.reading_extent: Bibliographic metadata only; whole book body unread.
rows.argument_assessment: The earlier article describes the planned book, which cannot substitute for reading the completed 1995 argument.
rows.endpoint_status: Anna Clark absent; no biography or edge proposed.

rows.citation: Sally Alexander, “Women, Class and Sexual Differences in the 1830 s and 1840 s: Some Reflections on the Writing of a Feminist History,” History Workshop Journal17(1)(Spring 1984),125–149.
rows.reading_extent: Original metadata and reprint contents only; substantive 1984 article/reprint text not read.
rows.argument_assessment: Feminist development is a lead, not yet a verified direct Jones criticism.
rows.endpoint_status: Sally Alexander absent; no automatic edge.

rows.citation: David Mayfield and Susan Thorne, “Social History and Its Discontents: Gareth Stedman Jones and the Politics of Language,” Social History17(2)( 1992),165–188.
rows.reading_extent: Original journal metadata/abstract and Lawrence–Taylor’s selected 1993 reply; original 1992 article body unread.
rows.argument_assessment: Lawrence–Taylor identify Mayfield and Thorne as their immediate opponents. Their account is named-reader mediation, not our fresh reading of the original argument.
rows.endpoint_status: David Mayfield and Susan Thorne absent; joint credit required.

rows.citation: Jon Lawrence and Miles Taylor, “The Poverty of Protest: Gareth Stedman Jones and the Politics of Language—a Reply,” Social History18(1)(January 1993),1–15.
rows.reading_extent: Fresh selected primary transcription pp. 1–3 and 10–15; not facsimile-collated.
rows.argument_assessment: Main target is Mayfield–Thorne. Specific Jones criticism remains, alongside defense against determinism.
rows.endpoint_status: jon_lawrence exists; Miles Taylor absent but equally credited.

rows.citation: Patrick Joyce, “The Imaginary Discontents of Social History: A Note of Response to Mayfield and Thorne, and Lawrence and Taylor,” Social History18(1)( 1993),81–85.
rows.reading_extent: Full title/publisher metadata only; primary reply body unread.
rows.argument_assessment: The title names Mayfield–Thorne AND Lawrence–Taylor as reply targets. It does not establish an anti-Jones argument.
rows.endpoint_status: patrick_joyce exists; no new direct Jones edge from metadata.

rows.citation: Gareth Stedman Jones, “The Determinist Fix: Some Obstacles to the Further Development of the Linguistic Approach to History in the 1990 s,” History Workshop Journal42(1)(Autumn 1996),19–35.
rows.reading_extent: Original publisher metadata checked; no substantive primary body or abstract read. Attempted anthology preview did not expose the chapter.
rows.argument_assessment: The claim that Jones partly answers Joyce/Vernon is NOT substantively verified here. Neither title nor later commentators suffice to assign that target or reconstruct his position.
rows.endpoint_status: Gareth exists; no new reverse criticism inferred.

rows.citation: Miles Taylor, “Rethinking the Chartists: Searching for Synthesis in the Historiography of Chartism,” The Historical Journal39(2)(June 1996),479–495.
rows.reading_extent: Bibliographic metadata only; primary body unread.
rows.argument_assessment: Review/synthesis title alone does not verify its adjudication of Jones or a consensus against him.
rows.endpoint_status: Miles Taylor absent; distinct from existing historians with surname Taylor.

rows.citation: Malcolm Chase, Chartism: A New History (Manchester University Press, 2007).
rows.reading_extent: Bibliographic metadata only; primary book body unread.
rows.argument_assessment: Later synthesis is not proof of universal consensus or a direct criticism until actual selected passages are checked.
rows.endpoint_status: Malcolm Chase absent; no new biography or edge.

access_limits: Publisher preview scans were OCR-assisted; the two proposed book passages were then visually collated.
Scribd supplies a third-party transcription of the 1993 primary reply, not an independently collated facsimile.
The Michigan Mayfield–Thorne 1990 working-paper URL returned an HTML challenge, not a PDF; draft not substituted for 1992 journal text.
Attempted 2005 Spiegel anthology preview/transcription did not provide verified Jones chapter reading.
OpenAlex remained paused. No raw primary body or image is stored in these tracked audit outputs.
